framework_note: BACKTEST cutoff 2022-06-01. J-Book corpus is sourced from FY2026 Pentagon books (PB submitted ~June 2025); at this historical cutoff, every PE/program lookup returns NOT_FOUND_IN_TIMERANGE because no FY26 budget rows are visible pre-2022-06-01. Per heuristic #7 + the prompt's preamble, J-Book NOT_FOUND at a 2022 cutoff is not a red flag — most J-Book de-fundings that materialized in 2024-2026 were not yet visible. Where J-Book returns NOT_FOUND_IN_TIMERANGE, we score UNVERIFIABLE and document the corpus-coverage gap. Where USAspending confirms the company received the claimed contracts, we treat the claim as PASS (the claim was real). NOTE: usaspending.query_dod_contracts does not appear to honor cutoff_date — returned awards include FY2024+ obligations. The cutoff_date kwarg is still passed per instruction but the data returned must be filtered mentally to pre-cutoff context. We only credit awards whose Award ID prefix pre-dates the cutoff (e.g., HR001118C0103 — DARPA R3D2 — is pre-cutoff and provides ground-truth support).

summary.overall_pattern: NO DIVERGENCE SIGNAL DETECTABLE AT 2022-06-01 CUTOFF. RKLB's pre-cutoff 10-K relies on broad agency-customer relationships (DoD, DARPA, NRO, NASA) and one specific NSSL/SSC aspiration — none of which is mapped to a specific PE-number-revenue claim that the J-Book corpus (FY2026 PB) can challenge. USAspending corroborates real pre-cutoff DoD contracts (R3D2). Cohort-metadata claims (STP-S30, SDA T3) materialized post-cutoff. At 2022 visibility this is a small-cap space company with thin but real defense pipeline + a coherent rollup; the framework correctly emits PASS/UNVERIFIABLE rather than manufacturing severity (per the prompt's calibration guidance for early-cutoff backtests). Honest 2022 verdict: no J-Book divergence pattern.
